title: Exercise 7B · Q5
summary: A screen size is its diagonal — the width is a shorter side.
alt: Exercise 7B · Q5: Mr Lee buys a 30-inch television. The height of the screen is 18 inches. Given that television screens are measured across the diagonal, i.e. the length of the diagonal is 30 inches, how wide is the screen?

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: Mr Lee buys a **30-inch television**: the diagonal **AC** of the screen is **30 inches**, and the height **BC** is **18 inches**. How wide is the screen (**AB**)?

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔABC, **∠B = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AC**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Make the unknown the subject
steps.narration: We want a **shorter side**, so subtract the known square from the hypotenuse square.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ \role{legA}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legB}{BC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ \role{legA}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{30^2} - \role{legB}{18^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ \role{legA}{AB^2} &= \role{hyp}{AC^2} - \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{30^2} - \role{legB}{18^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{900} - \role{legB}{324} \\ &= \role{legA}{576} \\ \role{legA}{AB} &= \sqrt{576} = \role{ans}{24\ \text{in}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse **17 in** and one shorter side **8 in**. Find the other shorter side.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find a shorter side: **subtract** the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the **square root**.
A shorter side must be **smaller** than the hypotenuse — a quick check on your answer.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.
